fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responders can confirm the correct property from the road.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles so emergency apparatus can reach both the main residence and the detached structure.
• Trim vegetation along the access drive so it does not narrow the driveway or obstruct the windshields and mirrors of responding apparatus.
• Cut back dense vegetation growing close to the main residence and detached structure so responders can move along exterior walls without obstruction.
• Keep a clear path between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move between buildings without pushing through vegetation.
• Mark or post the address visibly on both the main residence and the detached structure so responders can identify each building quickly on arrival.
• Keep the walkway from the driveway to the main entrance clear of stored items, overgrown plants, and debris.
• Identify and communicate to household members one designated staging area on the open lawn where responding units can park and set up without blocking the access drive.
• Because rear access is limited to a single point, avoid storing equipment, vehicles, or materials anywhere along the access drive that would prevent a second apparatus from reaching the rear of the property.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim back shrubs and low branches that are directly touching or within a few feet of the house on all sides.
• Thin the tree clusters near the structure so individual trees are more spread apart and not touching each other or the house.
• Remove low-hanging branches from large trees close to the house, cutting them up at least 10 feet from the ground.
• Clear shrubs and small plants growing beneath the large trees nearest the structure.
• Cut back or remove the mixed shrub and plant growth pressing against the sides of the house.
• Thin scattered trees and shrubs between the house and the tree clusters to break up the continuous path of vegetation leading to the structure.
• Trim branches overhanging the driveway so vehicles, including fire trucks, can pass through without obstruction.
• Clear shrubs and tall grass growing along both sides of the driveway for its full length.
• Keep the driveway surface free of fallen branches, leaves, and debris that could block access.
• Work to create a clear path around the rear of the structure to allow access from that side, even if limited.
• Remove or thin vegetation growing against or directly next to any outbuildings or detached structures on the property.
• Scatter or remove piled plant debris, cut branches, and leaf litter that may have accumulated near the house or along the driveway.
